docs.title: Workshop Template
docs.text:
Workshop Template is a starter kit for hosting workshops, similar in spirit to MIT Missing Semester. Instead of writing a worksheet in a Google Doc or a slide deck, the host builds a static website where every exercise, video, and discussion lives on a searchable page.

The complete workflow — from an empty repository to a bilingual (English / 简体中文) workshop site deployed on GitHub Pages — takes approximately ten minutes. No server or frontend framework is required; all content is written in Markdown.

docs.title: Why publish the worksheet as a website?
docs.text:
• A single link to share — participants always see the latest version; there is no need to redistribute PDFs after each revision.
  • Bilingual support out of the box — English and Chinese versions with a language switcher, suited to SSTIA workshops.
  • A built-in discussion board — each page can carry its own comment thread, powered by giscus and GitHub Discussions.
  • Rich media — images, videos, mathematical formulas, diagrams, and interactive widgets require no additional tooling.
  • Full-text search — participants can locate any topic quickly.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
1. Click Use this template on GitHub to create a repository.
  2. Enable GitHub Pages and push any commit — GitHub Actions builds and deploys the site automatically.
  3. Edit the Markdown files and commit. The site is live at https://<you>.github.io/<your-repo>/.

Detailed instructions are provided in Deploy with GitHub Pages.

docs.title: About
docs.text: Workshop Template is a starter kit for SSTIA workshop hosts. It packages a complete MkDocs + Material for MkDocs setup — bilingual build, GitHub Pages deployment, discussion board, and media support — so that a worksheet becomes a website within minutes.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Contributions are welcome. The CONTRIBUTING.md file describes the process; in short: open an issue to discuss the change, then submit a pull request. Every pull request runs the health check workflow (mkdocs build --strict).

docs.title: Discussion Board
docs.text: Each page can carry its own discussion thread. The board is powered by giscus, which stores comments as GitHub Discussions in the site's repository — participants sign in with their GitHub account, and the host moderates from the repository's Discussions tab.

docs.title: How the template wires it up
docs.text:
The template ships docs/overrides/comments.html, a Jinja template that renders the giscus widget only when the page sets discussions: true in its frontmatter:

YAML
---
discussions: true
---

This page carries that flag; the comment thread below is the live demonstration.

For the override to take effect, it must be included by a page template. Create docs/overrides/main.html with the following content:

HTML
{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block content %}
  {{ super() }}
  {% include "comments.html" %}
{% endblock %}

Explanation:

  • custom_dir: docs/overrides in mkdocs.yml makes MkDocs look for templates in docs/overrides/ first.
  • main.html extends the theme's base.html (which contains the full page skeleton).
  • {{ super() }} renders the normal page content; the {% include %} then appends the comment section after it.

Activation step

The template repository provides comments.html; if main.html is not present in docs/overrides/, the comment section is never rendered. Verify both files exist after copying the template.

docs.title: Pointing giscus at your repository
docs.text:
comments.html ships pre-configured for the template's original repository. For comments to work on a new site, the configuration must be updated:

  1. Make sure the repository is public, and enable Discussions: Settings → General → Features → Discussions.
  2. Install the giscus app: open github.com/apps/giscus and grant it access to the repository.
  3. Collect the configuration: open giscus.app, fill in the repository, pick a category (the default Announcements category works), and copy the four generated values.
  4. Edit docs/overrides/comments.html and replace the four data-* attributes:
HTML
data-repo="<you>/<your-repo>"
data-repo-id="R_..."
data-category="Announcements"
data-category-id="DIC_..."
Attribute Meaning data-repo / data-repo-id The repository that stores the discussions data-category / data-category-id The GitHub Discussions category threads are created in data-mapping="pathname" One thread per page URL data-strict="1" Only the exact URL matches — a page and its query strings do not share a thread data-reactions-enabled="1" Emoji reactions on comments data-input-position="bottom" Comment box below the existing comments data-theme Light/dark widget theme; set dynamically by the page script data-lang Widget interface language (en, zh-CN, …)

With data-mapping="pathname" and data-strict="1", every page owns one thread, created on first visit. The English page and its Chinese counterpart are separate URLs (/discussion/ vs /zh/discussion/) and therefore get separate threads.

docs.title: Theme synchronization
docs.text: comments.html includes a small script that watches the site's color scheme and sends the current theme to the giscus iframe, so the widget follows the light/dark toggle without configuration.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Comments work only after deployment. The widget needs the public repository and the real page URL; the local preview (http://localhost:8000) does not load comments.
  • Moderation happens in the repository's Discussions tab, where threads are ordinary discussion posts.
  • To disable the board on a page, remove discussions: true from its frontmatter.
  • Private repositories are not supported by giscus.

docs.title: Customization
docs.text: Beyond pages and colors, the template has four extension points: theme overrides, global CSS/JavaScript, build hooks, and additional plugins or Markdown extensions.

docs.title: Theme overrides
docs.text:
custom_dir: docs/overrides makes MkDocs look for templates in docs/overrides/ before falling back to the theme's own templates. A file there overrides the theme file of the same name.

The worked example is the discussion board: docs/overrides/main.html extends the theme and appends the comments section (see Discussion Board):

HTML
{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block content %}
  {{ super() }}
  {% include "comments.html" %}
{% endblock %}

The pattern generalizes to any block. A maintenance banner, for example, overrides the announce block:

HTML
{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block announce %}
  The worksheet is being updated; the new version arrives on Friday.
{% endblock %}

A custom footer overrides the footer block:

HTML
{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block footer %}
  <footer>Workshop materials © 2026 — <a href="mailto:you@example.com">contact</a></footer>
{% endblock %}

Block names can be found in the theme's base.html inside the installed package (.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/material/templates/).

docs.title: Global CSS and JavaScript
docs.text:
• extra_css loads a stylesheet on every page. Add the file under docs/assets/css/ (or docs/stylesheets/) and list it in mkdocs.yml:

    YAML
    extra_css:
  - assets/css/custom.css

  • extra_javascript loads a script on every page. The template already uses it for javascripts/mathjax.js (MathJax configuration), and the same mechanism serves custom widgets:

    YAML
    extra_javascript:
  - javascripts/mathjax.js
  - assets/js/my-widget.js

    Because the script loads on every page, use a guarded initializer that activates only where the widget's container exists:

    JavaScript
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  var root = document.getElementById("my-widget");
  if (root) initMyWidget(root);
});

    This is the production form of the inline game demonstrated on the Game Demo page.

docs.title: Build hooks
docs.text:
docs/scripts/hooks.py is registered under hooks: in mkdocs.yml. The template's hook runs after each build and copies sitemap.xml into the Chinese folder, so search engines receive the Chinese URLs as well:

Python
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

def on_post_build(config, **kwargs):
    site_dir = Path(config.site_dir)
    root_sitemap = site_dir / "sitemap.xml"
    if not root_sitemap.exists():
        return

    for lang in ["zh"]:
        lang_dir = site_dir / lang
        if lang_dir.is_dir():
            shutil.copy(root_sitemap, lang_dir / "sitemap.xml")

Hooks are plain Python functions named after MkDocs events (on_page_markdown, on_page_content, on_post_build, and others). Any such function defined in the file is picked up automatically. Examples: post-processing the rendered HTML of every page (on_page_content), or generating additional files after the build. The full event list is in the MkDocs documentation.

docs.title: More Markdown extensions
docs.text:
pymdownx.tasklist (checkboxes) and pymdownx.tabbed (content tabs) are enabled in the template; demos are provided on the Markdown Basics page. The procedure for adding further extensions is the same for all of them. pymdownx.keys, for example, renders keyboard-key combinations:

YAML
markdown_extensions:
  - pymdownx.keys
Markdown
Press ++ctrl+alt+delete++ to open the task manager.

These extensions all come from pymdown-extensions, which is already in requirements.txt, so no dependency change is needed.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
The enabled plugins:

Plugin Function search Full-text search (reconfigured per language by i18n) mkdocs-video ![type:video](…) embeds (see Images & Videos) i18n The bilingual build minify Minifies the built HTML

Two further plugins are installed but not enabled, kept as ready options:

  • mkdocs-redirects — old URLs redirect to new ones after a page is renamed or moved.
  • mkdocs-git-revision-date-localized-plugin — displays the last-updated date of each page (useful for worksheets).

Enabling either is a one-line addition to plugins: in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Theme features
docs.text: The features list under theme toggles Material behaviors. The template enables: navigation.tabs, navigation.sections, navigation.top, navigation.tracking, search.highlight, search.share, content.code.copy. Commonly useful additions include navigation.instant (faster page transitions), navigation.footer (prev/next links at the bottom), and content.code.annotate (annotations in code blocks). The full list is in the Material documentation.

docs.title: Custom domain
docs.text: GitHub Pages can serve a custom domain: Settings → Pages → Custom domain, then update site_url in mkdocs.yml accordingly.

docs.title: Game Demo
docs.text:
The md_in_html Markdown extension passes arbitrary HTML, CSS, and JavaScript through to the page. This makes worksheets interactive: exercises can be quizzes, simulators, or games that run directly in the browser.

The Snake game below is embedded in this page and uses no external code. It is deliberately small — one canvas, one loop — so the mechanism stays visible. Use the arrow keys (or W/A/S/D) to steer.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The widget has three parts, all written directly in the Markdown file:

  1. The container — an empty <div id="snake-game">. Its data-* attributes carry every visible label (score, restart, game-over message). The script reads them at startup, so the same code serves both languages: the Chinese version of this page passes Chinese labels, the code is identical.
  2. The styles — a <style> block scoped to the widget. The look is deliberately a minimal retro terminal: green-on-black, monospace, hard square borders, no animations. The widget uses its own fixed palette instead of the site theme; the alternative is to use Material's CSS variables (--md-primary-fg-color, --md-code-bg-color, …) so a widget follows the theme and dark mode.
  3. The script — a self-contained IIFE that draws the board on a canvas, runs the game loop with setInterval, reads the keyboard, and renders the score. No libraries, no build step.

The {score} placeholder in the game-over message is replaced by the script with the actual score.

docs.title: Extracting the code into a shared file
docs.text:
A widget that appears on several pages should not be duplicated. The production form keeps the container in the page and moves the styles and script to a shared file loaded once:

  1. Move the CSS and JS into docs/assets/js/my-widget.js (the JS creates the <style> element itself, or the CSS goes to docs/assets/css/ and is loaded via extra_css).

  2. Register the script globally:

    YAML
    extra_javascript:
  - assets/js/my-widget.js

  3. Use a guarded initializer so the script does nothing on pages without the container:

    JavaScript
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  var root = document.getElementById("my-widget");
  if (root) initMyWidget(root);
});

This is the pattern used by the template's own mathjax.js. See Customization for the configuration details.

docs.title: Ideas for worksheets
docs.text:
• A quiz with a score and localStorage persistence between sessions.
  • Flashcards for vocabulary or commands.
  • An embedded code runner via a CodePen or Replit <iframe> for programming exercises.
  • A small simulator (e.g. visualizing an algorithm) with a few buttons and a canvas.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Keep widgets dependency-free and small; they load on every visit.
  • Test the widget on both language versions — all visible text should come from the container's data-* attributes.
  • Interactive code runs in the visitor's browser. Do not embed secrets or API keys.
  • Script and style blocks are treated as raw content by the Markdown parser; avoid writing strings that could be mistaken for markup (e.g. a literal </script> inside the script).
  • The board is drawn on a canvas, which screen readers cannot read; in production, describe the controls in the surrounding text.

docs.title: Bilingual Support
docs.text: The template publishes two complete versions of the site: English at the site root, Chinese under /zh/. Both are produced from the same mkdocs build by the i18n plugin (mkdocs-static-i18n).

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The plugin runs with docs_structure: folder, which maps each language folder to its output location:

Source folder Built to URL docs/en/ site/ https://<you>.github.io/<repo>/ docs/zh/ site/zh/ https://<you>.github.io/<repo>/zh/

The plugin configuration:

YAML
plugins:
  - i18n:
      docs_structure: folder
      reconfigure_material: true
      reconfigure_search: true
      languages:
        - locale: en
          default: true
          name: English
          build: true
        - locale: zh
          name: 简体中文
          build: true
          nav_translations:
            Home: 首页
            About: 关于

The pieces:

  • docs_structure: folder — each language lives in its own folder inside docs/. The default language (en) builds to the site root; other languages build to /zh/.
  • default: true on en — the language whose content is used as a fallback (see below).
  • nav_translations — Chinese titles for the navigation. Every entry in nav can be translated here; entries without a translation keep their English title. Section titles (e.g. Getting Started) are translated the same way.
  • reconfigure_search: true — the search index is rebuilt for the Chinese site with the correct language settings.

The language switcher in the header comes from extra.alternate:

YAML
extra:
  alternate:
    - name: English
      link: .
      lang: en
    - name: 简体中文
      link: zh/
      lang: zh

The plugin rewrites these links for each language build, so the switcher always points at the matching page in the other language. The build log additionally warns that the link values should be absolute paths; this warning can be ignored — relative links are correct for GitHub Pages project sites, which live under /<repo>/ rather than at the domain root.

docs.title: Writing a page in both languages
docs.text:
1. Write docs/en/<path>.md.
  2. Create docs/zh/<path>.md with the same relative path, containing the translation.
  3. Add the Chinese title to nav_translations.

The build matches files by their path inside the language folder. Relative links inside the content (e.g. [next](../getting-started/deployment.md)) are rewritten per language, so both versions navigate within their own language. Files in docs/assets/ are shared: the same ../assets/images/… path works from either language.

docs.title: If a translation is missing
docs.text: The build does not fail when a page exists only in English. The Chinese URL serves the English content (the default-language fallback). This is convenient while translations are pending, but the Chinese site then shows English content for that page.

docs.title: The Chinese UI language
docs.text: The template sets reconfigure_material: true, so the theme follows each language: the Chinese pages get Chinese interface strings (search placeholder, table-of-contents title, and the like) and an <html lang="zh"> attribute. Setting it to false keeps the interface strings in English while the content remains bilingual.

docs.title: Adding a third language
docs.text:
1. Create the folder, e.g. docs/fr/, and translate the pages into it.
  2. Register the language in the plugin configuration (locale: fr, name: Français, build: true, nav_translations: …).
  3. Add an extra.alternate entry with link: fr/.
  4. Update docs/scripts/hooks.py: the on_post_build hook copies sitemap.xml into each non-default language folder and currently hardcodes the list ["zh"].

docs.title: Keeping translations in sync
docs.text:
• Every pull request runs mkdocs build --strict; pages that link to files missing in one language fail the check.
  • The fallback hides a missing page, so a translation can be added later without breaking the site.
  • A useful review habit: after changing the English page, check the corresponding Chinese page in the same pull request.

docs.title: Markdown Basics
docs.text: The template supports standard Markdown plus the extensions listed in markdown_extensions in mkdocs.yml (tables, task lists, content tabs, admonitions, emoji, LaTeX math, Mermaid diagrams, and raw HTML). Every example on this page is rendered by the site itself; the source is shown in collapsible blocks.

docs.title: Text basics
docs.text:
Markdown
# Heading level 1
## Heading level 2
### Heading level 3

**bold**, *italic*, ***both***, ~~strikethrough~~, `inline code`

- unordered item
- another item
    - nested item (4 spaces)

1. ordered item
2. another item

[internal link](../getting-started/deployment.md)
[external link](https://www.mkdocs.org/)

> A blockquote.

---

A hard line break needs  
two trailing spaces.
  • Headings #–###### generate the table of contents on the right; hovering a heading reveals a permalink (the ¶ symbol), which is useful for linking to a specific section of the worksheet.
  • Headings containing non-ASCII characters (e.g. Chinese) produce IDs with those characters stripped — often just a number such as #1. For stable, readable links, assign an explicit ID with the attribute syntax: ## Deploy steps {#deploy-steps}, then link with [jump](#deploy-steps).
  • Internal links use paths relative to the current file, e.g. ../getting-started/deployment.md. MkDocs converts them to the correct URL on every page, in both languages.
  • A blank line is required between block elements; two trailing spaces produce a line break inside a paragraph.

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
Command Function mkdocs serve Start a live preview server mkdocs build Build the static site into site/ mkdocs build --strict Build and fail on broken links Markdown
| Command | Function |
| --- | --- |
| `mkdocs serve` | Start a live preview server |
| `mkdocs build` | Build the static site into `site/` |
| `mkdocs build --strict` | Build and fail on broken links |

The second row (---) is mandatory; column widths are computed automatically. Alignment is set with colons in the separator row (:---, :---:, ---:).

docs.title: Code blocks
docs.text:
Python
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    """Return a friendly greeting."""
    return f"Hello, {name}!"
Markdown
```python
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    """Return a friendly greeting."""
    return f"Hello, {name}!"
```
  • Fenced blocks with a language tag get syntax highlighting; the copy button in the top-right corner is enabled by the content.code.copy theme feature.
  • To show a fence inside a code block (as above), use four backticks on the outer fence.

docs.title: Admonitions
docs.text:
A note with a custom title

Notes present supplementary information.

Tip

Tips suggest optional improvements.

Warning

Warnings describe actions that may cause problems.

Heads-up

Danger blocks flag destructive operations.

Markdown
!!! note "A note with a custom title"
    Notes present supplementary information.

!!! tip
    Tips suggest optional improvements.

!!! warning
    Warnings describe actions that may cause problems.

!!! danger "Heads-up"
    Danger blocks flag destructive operations.

Other supported types: info, success, failure, bug, example, and quote. The syntax is !!! type "optional title" followed by an indented body.

docs.title: Collapsible blocks
docs.text:
Solution — click to reveal

Hiding solutions behind collapsible blocks is a common pattern for worksheets.

Python
print("Hello, world!")
Markdown
??? example "Solution — click to reveal"
    Hiding solutions behind collapsible blocks is a common pattern for worksheets.

The block starts expanded with ???+ type instead of ??? type.

docs.title: Task lists
docs.text:
• Fork the template repository
  • Enable GitHub Pages
  • Write the worksheet
  • Announce the workshop
Markdown
- [x] Fork the template repository
- [x] Enable GitHub Pages
- [ ] Write the worksheet

Checkboxes are rendered by pymdownx.tasklist. They are read-only in the browser — the checked state comes from the source file — which makes them suited to reading checklists and progress tracking in a worksheet.

docs.title: Content tabs
docs.text:
Task

Create a page docs/en/my-exercise.md and register it in nav.

Solution

Tip

Do not forget the Chinese mirror in docs/zh/.

Markdown
=== "Task"
    Create a page `docs/en/my-exercise.md` and register it in `nav`.

=== "Solution"
    !!! tip
        Do not forget the Chinese mirror in `docs/zh/`.

Each === "Label" starts a tab; the content is indented by four spaces and may contain any Markdown, including admonitions and code blocks. Content tabs are typically used to hide solutions behind a click.

docs.title: Emoji
docs.text: The pymdownx.emoji extension renders shortcodes such as :smile: → and :rocket: → , as well as :material/rocket-launch: icons from the Material icon set. A reference of shortcodes is available at material icons search.

docs.title: Math
docs.text:
Inline math uses \( ... \): the mass–energy equivalence is \(E = mc^2\).

Display math uses \[ ... \]:

\[ \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} e^{-x^2} \, dx = \sqrt{\pi} \] Markdown
Inline math uses `\( ... \)`: the mass–energy equivalence is \(E = mc^2\).

Display math uses `\[ ... \]`:

\[
\int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} e^{-x^2} \, dx = \sqrt{\pi}
\]

The formula is rendered by MathJax (the pymdownx.arithmatex extension generates the markup, docs/javascripts/mathjax.js supplies the configuration). Dollar-sign delimiters ($...$) are not enabled by default.

docs.title: Diagrams
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Edit docs/] --> B[Commit & push]
    B --> C[GitHub Action builds]
    C --> D[Site updates]

docs.title: Raw HTML
docs.text:
The md_in_html extension passes HTML through to the page:

This paragraph is raw HTML inside Markdown. Markdown
<div style="border: 1px solid var(--md-typeset-table-color); border-radius: 4px; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; display: inline-block;">
This paragraph is raw HTML inside Markdown.
</div>

This is the mechanism behind embedded widgets and games; see the Game Demo for a complete example.

docs.title: Frontmatter
docs.text:
Each page may begin with a YAML block:

YAML
---
title: Browser-tab title          # optional; defaults to the H1
description: Summary for search results
discussions: true                 # enable the comment thread (see Discussion Board)
---

docs.title: More extensions
docs.text: This template has already enabled the most common extensions. Further extensions can be added the same way — see Customization, which walks through the pattern.

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
The standard Markdown image syntax is used:

Markdown
![alt text](../assets/images/image_demo.png)

The alt text describes the image for screen readers and is shown if the file cannot be loaded.

docs.title: Where to put files
docs.text: Place images in docs/assets/images/ (or subfolders). The assets/ directory is shared between the English and Chinese builds, and MkDocs rewrites relative paths automatically — ../assets/images/… works from a page in either language.

docs.title: Sizing
docs.text:
The attr_list extension attaches HTML attributes:

Markdown
![demo](../assets/images/image_demo.png){ width="300" }

docs.title: Captions
docs.text:
Wrap the image in a figure to add a caption:

Markdown
<figure markdown="span">
  ![The bundled demo image](../assets/images/image_demo.png){ width="480" }
  <figcaption>Figure 1 — The bundled demo image.</figcaption>
</figure>
Figure 1 — The bundled demo image.

The markdown="span" attribute tells the md_in_html extension to process the inner content as Markdown.

docs.title: External images
docs.text: Remote URLs work unchanged: ![alt](https://example.com/image.png). For images served from your own site, keep them in docs/assets/ so they survive renames and remain available offline.

docs.title: Videos
docs.text:
The mkdocs-video plugin converts an image tag whose alt text is type:video into an embedded player:

Markdown
![type:video](../assets/videos/video_demo.mp4)

This renders the 30-second bundled demo clip, docs/assets/videos/video_demo.mp4. Videos are placed in docs/assets/videos/, following the same convention as images.

docs.title: Controlling the player
docs.text:
Attributes attached with attr_list are copied onto the player. The plugin applies a default style (full width, 16:9-ish height); override it with a style attribute:

Markdown
![type:video](../assets/videos/video_demo.mp4){ style="width:640px;height:360px" }

To opt out of the plugin's default style entirely (e.g. to set only width/height attributes), add disable-global-config:

Markdown
![type:video](../assets/videos/video_demo.mp4){ disable-global-config width="640" height="360" }

docs.title: Native player controls
docs.text:
By default the plugin embeds the file in an <iframe>. Set is_video: true in the plugin configuration to use a native <video> element instead, which enables the global options video_autoplay, video_loop, video_muted, and video_controls:

YAML
plugins:
  - mkdocs-video:
      is_video: true
      video_autoplay: true
      video_loop: true
      video_muted: true

docs.title: External platforms
docs.text:
For YouTube, Bilibili, or similar platforms, paste the platform's embed <iframe> directly — the md_in_html extension passes it through:

Markdown
<iframe width="560" height="315"
  src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID"
  title="Video player" frameborder="0"
  allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"
  allowfullscreen></iframe>

docs.title: File size
docs.text:
GitHub Pages has no per-file limit beyond the repository's practical bounds, but large videos slow down cloning and page loads. A guideline:

  • under ~10 MB per video: store it in docs/assets/videos/;
  • above that: upload to an external host (YouTube, Bilibili, a cloud drive) and embed the link or iframe.

docs.title: Add a New Page
docs.text: Adding a page involves three steps: create the Markdown file, register it in nav, and provide the Chinese mirror. Each step is described below.

docs.title: Step 1 — Create the Markdown file
docs.text:
Create the file in the English folder, e.g. docs/en/authoring/example.md. The path determines the URL: docs/en/authoring/example.md becomes https://<you>.github.io/<your-repo>/authoring/example/.

Files can be created in the GitHub web editor (Add file → Create new file) or locally. Folder names use lowercase and hyphens, e.g. getting-started/.

Every page starts with optional frontmatter:

YAML
---
title: Example Page        # used for the browser tab; independent of the H1
description: A one-sentence summary shown in search results
discussions: true          # optional: enable the comment thread (see Discussion Board)
---

# Example Page

Page content starts here.

The title in frontmatter is metadata only; the visible heading is the # line in the body.

docs.title: Step 2 — Register the page in nav
docs.text:
MkDocs builds only pages listed in nav in mkdocs.yml. Add the page to the appropriate section:

YAML
nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Getting Started:
      - Introduction: getting-started/introduction.md
      - Deploy with GitHub Pages: getting-started/deployment.md
  - Authoring:
      - Add a New Page: authoring/new-pages.md
      - Example Page: authoring/example.md      # ← new entry
  - Discussion Board: discussion.md

Notes on this syntax:

  • - Title: path adds a page; the title appears in the sidebar and tabs.
  • Indented entries under a bare key (- Getting Started:) form a section with subpages.
  • The path is relative to the language folder — authoring/example.md means docs/en/authoring/example.md in the English build and docs/zh/authoring/example.md in the Chinese build. The language prefix is never written in nav.
  • Pages can appear in any order; the nav order defines the sidebar and prev/next navigation.

For the Chinese navigation to show a translated title, add it to nav_translations in the i18n plugin configuration:

YAML
plugins:
  - i18n:
      languages:
        - locale: zh
          nav_translations:
            Example Page: 示例页面

docs.title: Step 3 — Create the Chinese version
docs.text:
Create docs/zh/authoring/example.md with the same relative path, containing the translated content. The bilingual system matches files by path, so the two files must share their location inside their language folders.

If the Chinese file is missing, the build does not fail: the Chinese URL serves the English content instead. This fallback is convenient while a translation is in progress, but the nav item, content, and search results then appear in English on the Chinese site. Details: Bilingual Support.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Commit the changes. On the next build (or after mkdocs serve reloads):

  • the page appears in the navigation and the previous/next links;
  • /authoring/example/ serves the English version;
  • /zh/authoring/example/ serves the Chinese version;
  • the language switcher swaps between them.

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Step Action 1 Create docs/en/<path>.md 2 Add - Title: <path>.md to nav in mkdocs.yml; add the Chinese title to nav_translations 3 Create docs/zh/<path>.md with translated content

docs.title: Theme & Colors
docs.text:
Colors are configured in the theme.palette section of mkdocs.yml. The template ships with two palettes — one for light mode, one for dark mode — and the browser's color preference selects between them:

YAML
theme:
  palette:
    # Palette toggle for light mode
    - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: light)"
      scheme: default
      primary: indigo
      accent: indigo
      toggle:
        icon: material/brightness-7
        name: Switch to dark mode

    # Palette toggle for dark mode
    - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
      scheme: slate
      primary: cyan
      accent: cyan
      toggle:
        icon: material/brightness-4
        name: Switch to light mode

docs.title: What each setting does
docs.text:
Setting Function media CSS media query that activates this palette. prefers-color-scheme follows the visitor's OS setting; the header button switches manually scheme Base color scheme: default (light) or slate (dark) primary Main brand color — header, navigation tabs, table headers accent Secondary color — links, hover states, focus outlines toggle Icon and label of the light/dark switch in the header

The primary and accent values are Material color names (below). Colors rendered slightly differently in light and dark schemes; the scheme handles that automatically.

docs.title: Available colors
docs.text:
All Material colors below are valid values for primary and accent:

red pink purple deep purple indigo blue light blue cyan teal green light green lime yellow amber orange deep orange brown grey blue grey black / white

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Different colors per scheme. A teal/light-green identity:

YAML
palette:
  - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: light)"
    scheme: default
    primary: teal
    accent: light green
    toggle:
      icon: material/brightness-7
      name: Switch to dark mode
  - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
    scheme: slate
    primary: teal
    accent: light green
    toggle:
      icon: material/brightness-4
      name: Switch to light mode

Single dark theme. To serve dark mode only, keep one entry and remove the media key:

YAML
palette:
  - scheme: slate
    primary: cyan
    accent: cyan

Single light theme. The same with scheme: default. Without a second palette, the light/dark switch disappears from the header.

docs.title: Logo and favicon
docs.text:
Both are set under theme and live in docs/assets/:

YAML
theme:
  favicon: assets/favicon.svg
  logo: assets/logo.svg

Replace these two SVG files with the workshop's own branding; keeping the filenames means no configuration change. The logo appears in the header, the favicon in the browser tab.

docs.title: Beyond the palette
docs.text: Colors not covered by primary/accent (e.g. background tints or component borders) require custom CSS via extra_css and docs/overrides/; see Customization.

docs.title: Deploy with GitHub Pages
docs.text: This page describes the procedure for publishing the site, from an empty repository to a live deployment at https://<you>.github.io/<your-repo>/. The template performs the heavy lifting: a GitHub Actions workflow builds the site with MkDocs and publishes it to the gh-pages branch.

docs.title: Step 1 — Create a repository from the template
docs.text:
1. Open github.com/CedricHaskell/WorkshopTemplate.
  2. Click Use this template → Create a new repository.
  3. Choose a repository name. The name determines the site URL: git-workshop results in https://<you>.github.io/git-workshop/.
  4. Set visibility to Public. GitHub Pages on free accounts, and the giscus discussion board, both require a public repository.
  5. Click Create repository.

Why "Use this template" instead of "Fork"?

A fork retains a link to the original repository and does not run workflows until Actions is enabled manually. A template copy is an independent repository, which is preferable for a site that will be customized extensively.

docs.title: Step 2 — Grant the workflow permission to deploy
docs.text:
The publish workflow pushes the built site to the gh-pages branch using the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN. New repositories default to read-only token permissions; the write permission must be granted:

  1. Open Settings → Actions → General.
  2. Under Workflow permissions, select Read and write permissions.
  3. Click Save.

docs.title: Step 3 — Trigger the first build
docs.text:
Creating a repository from a template is not a push event, so the workflow has not yet run. Any commit triggers it:

  1. Open mkdocs.yml and click the pencil icon to edit.
  2. Change site_name: "Workshop Template" to the name of the workshop.
  3. Update site_url and repo_url at the same time; see Step 5.
  4. Commit the change (top-right button; e.g. chore: rename site).

The Actions tab then shows the publish site workflow. If the tab reports that workflows are disabled, use the button on that page to enable them.

docs.title: Step 4 — Point GitHub Pages at the gh-pages branch
docs.text:
The workflow builds the site into the gh-pages branch. GitHub Pages must be configured to serve it:

  1. Open Settings → Pages.
  2. Under Build and deployment → Source, select Deploy from a branch.
  3. Set Branch to gh-pages and the folder to / (root), then click Save.

The site is then available at https://<you>.github.io/<your-repo>/.

docs.title: Step 5 — Configure site identity
docs.text:
At minimum, update the following fields in mkdocs.yml:

YAML
site_name: "My Workshop"                    # shown in the header and the browser tab
site_description: "A workshop about ..."    # used for SEO
site_author: "Your Name"
site_url: "https://<you>.github.io/<your-repo>/"   # canonical URLs and the language switcher
repo_url: "https://github.com/<you>/<your-repo>"
repo_name: "<your-repo>"

The branding assets in docs/assets/ ship with the SSTIA logo. To use a custom logo, replace the following files:

  • logo.svg — the logo in the header, to the left of the site name
  • favicon.svg — the browser-tab icon

Finally, the discussion board must be pointed at the new repository. The template ships pre-configured for the original repository, so comments do not load on a copy until the configuration is updated. The procedure is described in Discussion Board.

docs.title: Local preview (optional)
docs.text:
For local editing with live reload:

Bash
git clone https://github.com/<you>/<your-repo>.git
cd <your-repo>
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

The preview is served at http://localhost:8000; saved changes reload the page automatically. The Chinese version is at http://localhost:8000/zh/.

  • mkdocs serve — live preview server (the command above)
  • mkdocs build — build the static site into site/ for inspection
  • mkdocs build --strict — build and fail on any broken link; this is what CI runs on pull requests

docs.title: The automation
docs.text:
Two workflows ship in .github/workflows/:

Workflow Trigger Function publish_site.yaml every push to main installs dependencies, runs mkdocs build, pushes site/ to the gh-pages branch health_check.yaml every pull request runs mkdocs build --strict; pull requests with broken links fail CI

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause and remedy Site returns 404 Pages is not yet pointed at gh-pages — perform Step 4 Workflow never runs No commit was pushed after repository creation, or Actions is disabled — see Step 3 Workflow fails at the deploy step Workflow permissions are read-only — see Step 2 Site is live but links are broken or point to the wrong domain site_url in mkdocs.yml still refers to the original template — update it (Step 5) Comments show an error on every page giscus is still configured for the template repository — see Discussion Board

docs.title: Intended audience
docs.text:
The template is intended for workshop hosts — instructors who design and run hands-on sessions such as hackathons, tutorials, or training courses. It addresses several recurring needs:

  • maintaining a worksheet in a version-controlled, shareable form;
  • distributing updated materials to participants without re-sending files;
  • providing a discussion space attached to the exercises;
  • maintaining English and Chinese versions of the same material.

It converts the worksheet into a static website, following the approach of MIT's Missing Semester: a single searchable site that contains all materials.

docs.title: Included features
docs.text: Feature Description Bilingual (EN / 中文) Two complete versions of every page, switchable from the header. The Chinese site is served under /zh/ One-push deploy A push to main triggers GitHub Actions, which builds the site and publishes it to GitHub Pages Rich Markdown Tables, code blocks, admonitions, task lists, content tabs, emoji, LaTeX math, and Mermaid diagrams Material theme The Material for MkDocs theme with light/dark modes, tabs, and search Images and videos Bundled demo files (image_demo.png, video_demo.mp4) demonstrate media embedding Discussion board Per-page comment threads powered by giscus and GitHub Discussions Interactive widgets The md_in_html extension allows arbitrary HTML/CSS/JS to be embedded — see the Game Demo CI health check Each pull request runs mkdocs build --strict, which fails on broken links

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
The requirements are minimal:

  • a GitHub account (free);
  • basic Markdown — familiarity with # Title and **bold** is sufficient for most of the work. The Markdown Basics page covers the rest.

Python is not required: all editing can be performed in the GitHub web editor, and Actions builds the site. A local Python environment is needed only for local preview.

docs.title: Organization of this documentation
docs.text:
The documentation forms a walkthrough, but each page is self-contained:

  1. Getting Started — deployment and repository layout (this section)
  2. Authoring — writing pages: Markdown, colors, media, bilingual content
  3. Discussion Board — comments for participants
  4. Advanced — customization: theme overrides, hooks, plugins, embedded widgets

The site hosting this documentation is built from the template. While reading, the repository can be consulted in parallel: every feature described here corresponds to real files in docs/ and mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Structure Overview
docs.text:
The complete repository layout:

Text Only
.
├── .github/workflows/
│   ├── publish_site.yaml      # push to main → build site → deploy to the gh-pages branch
│   └── health_check.yaml      # on PR → mkdocs build --strict (fails on broken links)
│
├── docs/                      # ← all content lives here
│   ├── en/                    # English source (the default language → site root)
│   │   ├── index.md           #   the home page
│   │   ├── about.md
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── zh/                    # Chinese source (→ /zh/ on the site)
│   │   ├── index.md           #   mirrors docs/en/ page by page
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── assets/                # shared static files (used by BOTH languages)
│   │   ├── images/image_demo.png    # sample image for the media tutorial
│   │   ├── videos/video_demo.mp4    # sample video for the media tutorial
│   │   ├── favicon.svg              # browser-tab icon
│   │   └── logo.svg                 # header logo
│   ├── javascripts/
│   │   └── mathjax.js         # MathJax configuration (loaded on every page)
│   ├── overrides/
│   │   └── comments.html      # giscus discussion board template (see Discussion Board)
│   └── scripts/
│       └── hooks.py           # build hooks, e.g. copying sitemap.xml into /zh/
│
├── mkdocs.yml                 # ← the central configuration: nav, theme, plugins, i18n
├── requirements.txt           # pinned Python dependencies (used by CI and local development)
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
├── LICENSE
└── README.md

docs.title: The two halves: docs/ and mkdocs.yml
docs.text:
• docs/ contains content — Markdown files and assets.
  • mkdocs.yml contains everything else — site name, theme, colors, plugins, and navigation. When the GitHub Action runs mkdocs build, it reads this file and converts docs/ into the static site in site/.

docs.title: Inside mkdocs.yml
docs.text: Section Function site_name / site_url / repo_url Site identity, canonical URLs, repository link theme Material theme configuration: light/dark palette, navigation features (tabs, top button, search), logo/favicon, and custom_dir pointing at docs/overrides markdown_extensions The Markdown dialect: tables, math, emoji, Mermaid fences, admonitions — everything demonstrated on the Markdown Basics page extra alternate — the language switcher entries (English → ., 简体中文 → zh/); plus global JavaScript (MathJax, Mermaid) plugins search (full-text), mkdocs-video (video embeds), i18n (bilingual build), minify (smaller HTML) nav The navigation, which defines the site structure. Only pages listed here are built.

docs.title: How the bilingual build works
docs.text:
The i18n plugin (mkdocs-static-i18n) is configured with docs_structure: folder:

Text Only
docs/en/**  --(default language)-->  site/**      (the English site)
docs/zh/**  ---------------------->  site/zh/**   (the Chinese site)

Two consequences follow:

  1. nav paths are language-relative. The entry Home: index.md resolves to docs/en/index.md in the English build and to docs/zh/index.md in the Chinese build. Languages never appear in the navigation.
  2. docs/assets/ is shared. Both language builds reference it; MkDocs rewrites relative paths automatically, so an image referenced from a Chinese page correctly points up to the shared assets/ folder. Writing ../assets/images/… works from either language.

The Chinese navigation titles come from nav_translations in the plugin configuration; the language switcher comes from extra.alternate. Details are provided in Bilingual Support.

docs.title: Additional notes
docs.text:
• Pages not listed in nav are not built. MkDocs renders only files reachable from the navigation, so a new page appears only after registration in mkdocs.yml; see Add a New Page.
  • Everything in docs/ is copied into the site. This is why docs/scripts/hooks.py and docs/overrides/ also end up in the published site/ folder. It is harmless, but any private script placed in docs/ will be public.

docs.title: Workshop Template
docs.text:
Workshop Template 是一个面向 workshop 的网站模板，思路类似 MIT Missing Semester：主讲人不再用 Google Doc 或幻灯片编写讲义，而是把讲义构建成一个静态网站，所有练习、视频和讨论都集中在一个可搜索的页面上。

从空仓库到部署在 GitHub Pages 上的双语（English / 简体中文）网站，整个过程大约需要十分钟。无需服务器、无需前端框架，内容全部使用 Markdown 编写。

docs.title: 为什么把讲义做成网站？
docs.text:
• 只需分享一个链接——参与者看到的永远是最新版本，不必在每次修改后重新分发 PDF。
  • 开箱即用的双语支持——英文与中文两个版本通过语言切换器互通，适合 SSTIA 的 workshop。
  • 内置讨论区——每个页面可以有自己的评论线程，由 giscus 与 GitHub Discussions 提供支持。
  • 丰富的媒体形式——图片、视频、数学公式、图表以及交互式组件都不需要额外工具。
  • 全文搜索——参与者可以快速定位任何内容。

docs.title: 快速开始
docs.text:
1. 在 GitHub 上点击 Use this template 创建自己的仓库。
  2. 启用 GitHub Pages 并推送任意一次提交——GitHub Actions 会自动构建并部署网站。
  3. 编辑 Markdown 文件并提交，网站即上线于 https://<you>.github.io/<your-repo>/。

详细步骤见部署到 GitHub Pages。

docs.title: 文档目录
docs.text: 主题 内容 模板介绍 模板的用途与适用人群 部署到 GitHub Pages 从零到上线，大约十分钟 结构总览 仓库与 mkdocs.yml 的组织方式 新建页面 创建页面并注册到导航 Markdown 基础 支持的语法：表格、公式、图表、提示框 主题与配色 配色方案、Logo 与图标 图片与视频 嵌入媒体，包括模板自带的示例 双语支持 中英双语系统的运作方式 讨论区 使用 giscus 为页面添加评论 自定义 主题覆盖、构建钩子、插件 小游戏 Demo 在页面中嵌入交互式组件

docs.title: 一个可运行的示例
docs.text:
本站完全由模板构建，没有任何额外代码。布局、配色、语言切换器、搜索栏以及内嵌的示例组件，全部来自 GitHub 仓库 中的文件。English version 展示双语系统的效果。

建议从以下页面开始：

  • 部署到 GitHub Pages —— 发布自己的站点
  • Markdown 基础 —— 编写讲义
  • 主题与配色 —— 调整站点外观

基于 MkDocs 与 Material for MkDocs 构建，由 GitHub Actions 部署，评论功能由 giscus 提供。

docs.title: 关于
docs.text: Workshop Template 是面向 SSTIA workshop 主讲人的起始模板。它打包了一套完整的 MkDocs + Material for MkDocs 配置——双语构建、GitHub Pages 部署、讨论区与媒体支持——让讲义在几分钟内变成一个网站。

docs.title: 作者
docs.text: 模板由 Cedric Haskell 维护。问题与建议可以在 GitHub issues 中提出。

docs.title: 许可证
docs.text: 模板以 MIT License 发布，见 LICENSE。

docs.title: 贡献
docs.text: 欢迎贡献。流程见 CONTRIBUTING.md，简而言之：先开 issue 讨论修改内容，再提交 pull request。每个 pull request 都会运行健康检查（mkdocs build --strict）。

docs.title: 讨论区
docs.text: 每个页面都可以有自己的讨论线程。讨论区由 giscus 提供支持，评论以 GitHub Discussions 的形式存放在站点仓库中——参与者用 GitHub 账号登录发言，主讲人在仓库的 Discussions 标签页中进行管理。

docs.title: 模板如何接线
docs.text:
模板附带 docs/overrides/comments.html，这是一个 Jinja 模板，仅当页面 frontmatter 中设置 discussions: true 时才渲染 giscus 组件：

YAML
---
discussions: true
---

本页就带有该标记；下方的评论线程是现场演示。

要让该覆盖生效，必须由页面模板将其引入。创建 docs/overrides/main.html，内容如下：

HTML
{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block content %}
  {{ super() }}
  {% include "comments.html" %}
{% endblock %}

说明：

  • mkdocs.yml 中的 custom_dir: docs/overrides 让 MkDocs 优先在 docs/overrides/ 中查找模板。
  • main.html 继承主题的 base.html（其中包含完整的页面骨架）。
  • {{ super() }} 渲染正常的页面内容；随后的 {% include %} 在内容之后追加评论区。

激活步骤

模板仓库提供了 comments.html；如果 docs/overrides/ 中没有 main.html，评论区不会被渲染。复制模板后请确认两个文件都存在。

docs.title: 把 giscus 指向你的仓库
docs.text:
comments.html 出厂时配置的是模板的原仓库。要让评论在新站点上工作，必须更新配置：

  1. 确认仓库为公开，并启用 Discussions：Settings → General → Features → Discussions。
  2. 安装 giscus 应用：打开 github.com/apps/giscus，授予它访问仓库的权限。
  3. 获取配置：打开 giscus.app，填写仓库，选择一个分类（默认的 Announcements 分类即可），复制生成的四个值。
  4. 编辑 docs/overrides/comments.html，替换四个 data-* 属性：
HTML
data-repo="<you>/<your-repo>"
data-repo-id="R_..."
data-category="Announcements"
data-category-id="DIC_..."
属性 含义 data-repo / data-repo-id 存放讨论的仓库 data-category / data-category-id 创建线程所用的 GitHub Discussions 分类 data-mapping="pathname" 每个页面 URL 一条线程 data-strict="1" 只有完全相同的 URL 才匹配——页面与其查询参数不共享线程 data-reactions-enabled="1" 评论的表情回应 data-input-position="bottom" 评论输入框位于已有评论下方 data-theme 组件的明暗主题；由页面脚本动态设置 data-lang 组件界面语言（en、zh-CN 等）

使用 data-mapping="pathname" 与 data-strict="1" 时，每个页面独占一条线程，首次访问时创建。英文页面与其中文对应页是不同 URL（/discussion/ 与 /zh/discussion/），因此各有一条线程。

docs.title: 主题同步
docs.text: comments.html 内置一段小脚本，监听站点的明暗方案并把当前主题发送给 giscus iframe，因此组件会跟随明暗切换，无需配置。

docs.title: 注意事项
docs.text:
• 评论只在部署后可用。 组件需要公开仓库与真实的页面 URL；本地预览（http://localhost:8000）不会加载评论。
  • 管理在仓库的 Discussions 标签页进行，线程就是普通的讨论帖。
  • 在页面上禁用讨论区：从 frontmatter 中移除 discussions: true。
  • giscus 不支持私有仓库。

docs.title: 自定义
docs.text: 除页面与配色之外，模板有四个扩展点：主题覆盖、全局 CSS/JavaScript、构建钩子，以及额外的插件或 Markdown 扩展。

docs.title: 主题覆盖
docs.text:
custom_dir: docs/overrides 让 MkDocs 优先在 docs/overrides/ 中查找模板，找不到时才回退到主题自带模板。目录中的文件会覆盖同名主题文件。

现成的例子是讨论区：docs/overrides/main.html 继承主题并追加评论区（见讨论区）：

HTML
{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block content %}
  {{ super() }}
  {% include "comments.html" %}
{% endblock %}

该模式适用于任意 block。例如维护公告横幅覆盖 announce block：

HTML
{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block announce %}
  讲义正在更新，新版本将于周五发布。
{% endblock %}

自定义页脚覆盖 footer block：

HTML
{% extends "base.html" %}

{% block footer %}

block 名称见主题安装目录中的 base.html（.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/material/templates/）。

docs.title: 全局 CSS 与 JavaScript
docs.text:
• extra_css 在每个页面加载样式表。把文件放在 docs/assets/css/（或 docs/stylesheets/）下，并在 mkdocs.yml 中登记：

    YAML
    extra_css:
  - assets/css/custom.css

  • extra_javascript 在每个页面加载脚本。模板已用它加载 javascripts/mathjax.js（MathJax 配置），自定义组件使用同一机制：

    YAML
    extra_javascript:
  - javascripts/mathjax.js
  - assets/js/my-widget.js

    由于脚本会在每个页面加载，需要使用守卫式初始化，只在组件容器存在的页面上激活：

    JavaScript
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  var root = document.getElementById("my-widget");
  if (root) initMyWidget(root);
});

    这正是小游戏 Demo 页面中内嵌游戏的生产化形式。

docs.title: 构建钩子
docs.text:
docs/scripts/hooks.py 通过 mkdocs.yml 中的 hooks: 注册。模板的钩子在每次构建后运行，把 sitemap.xml 复制进中文目录，使搜索引擎也能获得中文 URL：

Python
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

def on_post_build(config, **kwargs):
    site_dir = Path(config.site_dir)
    root_sitemap = site_dir / "sitemap.xml"
    if not root_sitemap.exists():
        return

    for lang in ["zh"]:
        lang_dir = site_dir / lang
        if lang_dir.is_dir():
            shutil.copy(root_sitemap, lang_dir / "sitemap.xml")

钩子是以 MkDocs 事件命名的普通 Python 函数（on_page_markdown、on_page_content、on_post_build 等）。文件中定义的任何这类函数都会被自动调用。典型用途：对每个页面渲染后的 HTML 做后处理（on_page_content），或在构建后生成额外文件。完整事件列表见 MkDocs 文档。

docs.title: 小游戏 Demo
docs.text:
md_in_html 扩展会把任意 HTML、CSS 与 JavaScript 原样传递到页面。这让讲义具备交互性：练习可以是测验、模拟器或直接运行在浏览器中的游戏。

下面的贪吃蛇游戏内嵌于本页，不使用任何外部代码。代码刻意保持精简——一个 canvas、一个循环——以便看清机制。用方向键（或 W/A/S/D）控制方向。

docs.title: 工作原理
docs.text:
组件由三部分组成，全部直接写在 Markdown 文件中：

  1. 容器 —— 一个空的 <div id="snake-game">。它的 data-* 属性承载所有可见文字（得分、重新开始、结束提示）。脚本在启动时读取这些属性，因此同一份代码服务两种语言：本页的中文版传入中文标签，代码完全一致。
  2. 样式 —— 一个作用于组件的 <style> 块。外观刻意采用极简复古终端风格：黑底绿字、等宽字体、硬直角边框、无动画。组件使用自己的固定配色而不跟随站点主题；另一种做法是使用 Material 的 CSS 变量（--md-primary-fg-color、--md-code-bg-color 等）让组件跟随主题与明暗模式。
  3. 脚本 —— 一个自包含的 IIFE，在 canvas 上绘制棋盘，用 setInterval 驱动游戏循环，读取键盘输入并渲染得分。无任何库、无构建步骤。

结束提示中的 {score} 占位符会被脚本替换为实际得分。

docs.title: 把代码抽取到共享文件
docs.text:
出现在多个页面上的组件不应重复复制。生产化的形式是：容器留在页面中，样式与脚本移入只加载一次的共享文件：

  1. 把 CSS 与 JS 移入 docs/assets/js/my-widget.js（JS 自行创建 <style> 元素；或把 CSS 放入 docs/assets/css/ 并通过 extra_css 加载）。

  2. 全局注册脚本：

    YAML
    extra_javascript:
  - assets/js/my-widget.js

  3. 使用守卫式初始化，让脚本在缺少容器的页面上什么都不做：

    JavaScript
    document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  var root = document.getElementById("my-widget");
  if (root) initMyWidget(root);
});

模板自带的 mathjax.js 用的就是这一模式。配置细节见自定义。

docs.title: 讲义中的用法
docs.text:
• 带得分与 localStorage 跨会话记忆的测验。
  • 词汇或命令的闪卡。
  • 通过 CodePen 或 Replit 的 <iframe> 内嵌代码运行器，用于编程练习。
  • 用少量按钮与 canvas 实现的小型模拟器（例如算法可视化）。

docs.title: 注意事项
docs.text:
• 组件保持零依赖、体积小；它们随每次访问加载。
  • 在两种语言版本上都测试组件——所有可见文字都应来自容器的 data-* 属性。
  • 交互代码运行在访问者的浏览器中，不要嵌入密钥或 API key。
  • 脚本与样式块被 Markdown 解析器视为原始内容；避免写出可能被误认为标记的字符串（例如脚本中出现字面的 </script>）。
  • 棋盘绘制在 canvas 上，屏幕阅读器无法读取；正式使用时，应在周围文字中说明操作方式。

docs.title: 双语支持
docs.text: 模板发布站点的两个完整版本：英文位于站点根目录，中文位于 /zh/ 下。两者由同一次 mkdocs build 通过 i18n 插件（mkdocs-static-i18n）生成。

docs.title: 工作原理
docs.text:
插件以 docs_structure: folder 模式运行，把每个语言目录映射到对应的输出位置：

源目录 构建到 URL docs/en/ site/ https://<you>.github.io/<repo>/ docs/zh/ site/zh/ https://<you>.github.io/<repo>/zh/

插件配置：

YAML
plugins:
  - i18n:
      docs_structure: folder
      reconfigure_material: true
      reconfigure_search: true
      languages:
        - locale: en
          default: true
          name: English
          build: true
        - locale: zh
          name: 简体中文
          build: true
          nav_translations:
            Home: 首页
            About: 关于

各项说明：

  • docs_structure: folder —— 每种语言在 docs/ 中拥有自己的目录。默认语言（en）构建到站点根目录；其他语言构建到 /zh/。
  • en 上的 default: true —— 该语言的内容用作回退源（见下文）。
  • nav_translations —— 导航的中文标题。nav 中的每个条目都可以在此翻译；未翻译的条目保留英文标题。小节标题（如 Getting Started）的翻译方式相同。
  • reconfigure_search: true —— 中文站点的搜索索引会按正确的语言设置重建。

页头的语言切换器来自 extra.alternate：

YAML
extra:
  alternate:
    - name: English
      link: .
      lang: en
    - name: 简体中文
      link: zh/
      lang: zh

插件会为每种语言的构建重写这些链接，因此切换器始终指向另一语言中的对应页面。构建日志还会警告 link 值应为绝对路径；这一警告可以忽略——GitHub Pages 项目站点位于 /<repo>/ 下而非域名根，相对链接才是正确的。

docs.title: 用两种语言写页面
docs.text:
1. 编写 docs/en/<path>.md。
  2. 以相同的相对路径创建 docs/zh/<path>.md，内容为翻译稿。
  3. 把中文标题加入 nav_translations。

构建按文件在语言目录内的路径进行匹配。内容中的相对链接（如 [下一页](../getting-started/deployment.md)）会按语言重写，两个版本都在各自语言内导航。docs/assets/ 中的文件是共享的：同一条 ../assets/images/… 路径在两种语言下都有效。

docs.title: 翻译缺失时的行为
docs.text: 页面只有英文版本时，构建不会失败。中文 URL 会回退到英文内容（默认语言回退）。翻译未完成时这一行为很方便，但该页面在中文站点会显示英文内容。

docs.title: 中文界面语言
docs.text: 模板设置了 reconfigure_material: true，主题会跟随各语言：中文页面获得中文界面文字（搜索框提示、目录标题等），以及 <html lang="zh"> 属性。把它改为 false 则界面文字保持英文，内容仍为双语。

docs.title: 添加第三种语言
docs.text:
1. 创建目录，如 docs/fr/，并翻译页面。
  2. 在插件配置中注册该语言（locale: fr、name: Français、build: true、nav_translations: …）。
  3. 添加 extra.alternate 条目，link: fr/。
  4. 更新 docs/scripts/hooks.py：on_post_build 钩子会把 sitemap.xml 复制到每个非默认语言目录，目前硬编码了列表 ["zh"]。

docs.title: 保持翻译同步
docs.text:
• 每个 pull request 都会运行 mkdocs build --strict；页面链接到某种语言中不存在的文件时检查会失败。
  • 回退机制掩盖了缺失的页面，因此翻译可以后补而不影响站点。
  • 建议的检查习惯：修改英文页面后，在同一个 pull request 中检查对应的中文页面。

docs.title: Markdown 基础
docs.text: 模板支持标准 Markdown 以及 mkdocs.yml 的 markdown_extensions 中列出的扩展（表格、任务列表、内容标签页、提示框、emoji、LaTeX 公式、Mermaid 图表与原生 HTML）。本页的每个示例都由站点实际渲染，源代码放在可折叠块中。

docs.title: 文本基础
docs.text:
Markdown
# 一级标题
## 二级标题
### 三级标题

**加粗**，*斜体*，***加粗斜体***，~~删除线~~，`行内代码`

- 无序列表项
- 另一项
    - 嵌套项（缩进 4 个空格）

1. 有序列表项
2. 另一项

[内部链接](../getting-started/deployment.md)
[外部链接](https://www.mkdocs.org/)

> 引用块。

---

段落内换行需要  
两个尾随空格。
  • # 到 ###### 生成右侧的目录；悬停在标题上会出现永久链接（¶ 符号），便于链接到讲义的某一小节。
  • 中文标题生成的锚点 ID 会被丢弃全部非 ASCII 字符（例如"第 1 步"的 ID 是 #1）。需要稳定、可读的链接时，用属性语法显式指定 ID：## 部署步骤 {#deploy-steps}，随后即可用 [跳转](#deploy-steps) 引用。
  • 内部链接使用相对当前文件的路径，如 ../getting-started/deployment.md。MkDocs 会在每个页面上、在两种语言中把它转换成正确的 URL。
  • 块级元素之间需要空行；段内换行使用两个尾随空格。

docs.title: 表格
docs.text:
命令 作用 mkdocs serve 启动实时预览服务器 mkdocs build 构建静态站点到 site/ mkdocs build --strict 构建并在链接失效时报错 Markdown
| 命令 | 作用 |
| --- | --- |
| `mkdocs serve` | 启动实时预览服务器 |
| `mkdocs build` | 构建静态站点到 `site/` |
| `mkdocs build --strict` | 构建并在链接失效时报错 |

第二行（---）必不可少；列宽自动计算。对齐方式在分隔行中用冒号设置（:---、:---:、---:）。

docs.title: 代码块
docs.text:
Python
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    """返回一句问候。"""
    return f"Hello, {name}!"
Markdown
```python
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    """返回一句问候。"""
    return f"Hello, {name}!"
```
  • 带语言标记的围栏代码块会获得语法高亮；右上角的复制按钮由 content.code.copy 主题特性提供。
  • 要在代码块中展示围栏本身（如上例），外层围栏使用四个反引号。

docs.title: 提示框
docs.text:
带自定义标题的 note

Note 用于补充信息。

Tip

Tip 用于可选的改进建议。

Warning

Warning 描述可能引起问题的操作。

注意

Danger 用于标记破坏性操作。

Markdown
!!! note "带自定义标题的 note"
    Note 用于补充信息。

!!! tip
    Tip 用于可选的改进建议。

!!! warning
    Warning 描述可能引起问题的操作。

!!! danger "注意"
    Danger 用于标记破坏性操作。

其他可用类型：info、success、failure、bug、example、quote。语法为 !!! 类型 "可选标题" 加缩进的正文。

docs.title: 可折叠块
docs.text:
解答——点击展开

把解答藏在可折叠块中是讲义中常见的做法。

Python
print("Hello, world!")
Markdown
??? example "解答——点击展开"
    把解答藏在可折叠块中是讲义中常见的做法。

使用 ???+ 类型 可以让块默认展开。

创建页面 docs/en/my-exercise.md，并注册到 nav。

解答

Tip

docs.title: 数学公式
docs.text:
行内公式使用 \( ... \)：质能方程是 \(E = mc^2\)。

\[ \int_{-\infty}^{+\infty} e^{-x^2} \, dx = \sqrt{\pi} \] Markdown

docs.text:
mkdocs-video 插件把 alt 文本为 type:video 的图片标签转换为内嵌播放器：

![type:video](../assets/videos/video_demo.mp4)

docs.title: 控制播放器
docs.text:
通过 attr_list 附加的属性会复制到播放器上。插件默认应用一套样式（全宽、约 16:9 的高度）；用 style 属性覆盖：

要完全放弃插件的默认样式（例如只设置 width/height 属性），加上 disable-global-config：

Markdown
![type:video](../assets/videos/video_demo.mp4){ disable-global-config width="640" height="360" }

docs.title: 原生播放器控件
docs.text:
插件默认用 <iframe> 嵌入文件。在插件配置中设置 is_video: true 可改用原生 <video> 元素，此时全局选项 video_autoplay、video_loop、video_muted、video_controls 生效：

YAML
plugins:
  - mkdocs-video:
      is_video: true
      video_autoplay: true
      video_loop: true
      video_muted: true

docs.title: 外部平台
docs.text:
对于 YouTube、Bilibili 等平台，直接粘贴平台提供的 <iframe> 嵌入代码——md_in_html 扩展会原样传递：

Markdown
<iframe width="560" height="315"
  src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/VIDEO_ID"
  title="Video player" frameborder="0"
  allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture"
  allowfullscreen></iframe>

docs.title: 文件大小
docs.text:
GitHub Pages 对单个文件没有硬性限制，但大视频会拖慢克隆与页面加载。建议：

  • 单个视频约 10 MB 以内：存放在 docs/assets/videos/；
  • 超过该大小：上传到外部平台（YouTube、Bilibili、云盘），嵌入链接或 iframe。

docs.title: 新建页面
docs.text: 添加页面分三步：创建 Markdown 文件、在 nav 中注册、提供中文版本。以下逐一说明。

docs.title: 第 1 步——创建 Markdown 文件
docs.text:
在英文目录中创建文件，例如 docs/en/authoring/example.md。文件路径决定 URL：docs/en/authoring/example.md 对应 https://<you>.github.io/<your-repo>/authoring/example/。

文件可以在 GitHub 网页编辑器中创建（Add file → Create new file），也可以在本地创建。目录名使用小写与连字符，例如 getting-started/。

每个页面以可选的 frontmatter 开头：

YAML
---
title: Example Page        # 浏览器标签页标题；与正文 H1 无关
description: 一句话摘要，显示在搜索结果中
discussions: true          # 可选：开启评论线程（见讨论区）
---

# Example Page

正文从这里开始。

frontmatter 中的 title 只是元数据；可见的标题是正文里的 # 行。

docs.title: 第 2 步——把页面注册到 nav
docs.text:
MkDocs 只构建 mkdocs.yml 的 nav 中列出的页面。把新页面加入对应小节：

YAML
nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Getting Started:
      - Introduction: getting-started/introduction.md
      - Deploy with GitHub Pages: getting-started/deployment.md
  - Authoring:
      - Add a New Page: authoring/new-pages.md
      - Example Page: authoring/example.md      # ← 新条目
  - Discussion Board: discussion.md

语法说明：

  • - 标题: 路径 添加一个页面；标题显示在侧边栏与标签页中。
  • 在纯键（如 - Getting Started:）下缩进的条目构成一个小节及其子页面。
  • 路径相对于语言目录——authoring/example.md 在英文构建中表示 docs/en/authoring/example.md，在中文构建中表示 docs/zh/authoring/example.md。语言前缀从不写入 nav。
  • 页面顺序任意；nav 的顺序决定侧边栏与上一页/下一页导航。

要让中文导航显示翻译后的标题，把它加入 i18n 插件配置中的 nav_translations：

YAML
plugins:
  - i18n:
      languages:
        - locale: zh
          nav_translations:
            Example Page: 示例页面

docs.title: 第 3 步——创建中文版本
docs.text:
以相同的相对路径创建 docs/zh/authoring/example.md，内容为翻译稿。双语系统按路径匹配文件，因此两个文件在各自语言目录内的位置必须一致。

如果中文文件缺失，构建不会失败：中文 URL 会回退到英文内容。翻译未完成时这一回退很方便，但该页面在中文站点的导航、内容与搜索结果中会显示英文。详见双语支持。

docs.title: 验证
docs.text:
提交修改。下一次构建（或 mkdocs serve 刷新）后：

  • 页面出现在导航与上一页/下一页链接中；
  • /authoring/example/ 提供英文版本；
  • /zh/authoring/example/ 提供中文版本；
  • 语言切换器可以在两者之间切换。

docs.title: 小结
docs.text: 步骤 操作 1 创建 docs/en/<path>.md 2 在 mkdocs.yml 的 nav 中添加 - 标题: <path>.md；把中文标题加入 nav_translations 3 创建 docs/zh/<path>.md，内容为翻译稿

docs.title: 主题与配色
docs.text:
配色在 mkdocs.yml 的 theme.palette 段中配置。模板自带两套 palette——一套用于浅色模式，一套用于深色模式——由浏览器的颜色偏好自动选择：

YAML
theme:
  palette:
    # Palette toggle for light mode
    - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: light)"
      scheme: default
      primary: indigo
      accent: indigo
      toggle:
        icon: material/brightness-7
        name: Switch to dark mode

    # Palette toggle for dark mode
    - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
      scheme: slate
      primary: cyan
      accent: cyan
      toggle:
        icon: material/brightness-4
        name: Switch to light mode

docs.title: 各配置项的含义
docs.text:
配置项 作用 media 激活该 palette 的 CSS 媒体查询。prefers-color-scheme 跟随访问者的系统设置；页头按钮可手动切换 scheme 基础配色方案：default（浅色）或 slate（深色） primary 主品牌色——页头、导航标签页、表头 accent 辅色——链接、悬停状态、焦点轮廓 toggle 页头明暗切换按钮的图标与文字

primary 与 accent 的取值是 Material 颜色名（见下表）。颜色在浅色与深色方案下渲染略有差异，scheme 会自动处理。

docs.title: 可用颜色
docs.text:
以下 Material 颜色都可以用作 primary 和 accent：

red pink purple deep purple indigo blue light blue cyan teal green light green lime yellow amber orange deep orange brown grey blue grey black / white

docs.title: 示例
docs.text:
两种方案使用不同配色。 以 teal/light green 为例：

YAML
palette:
  - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: light)"
    scheme: default
    primary: teal
    accent: light green
    toggle:
      icon: material/brightness-7
      name: Switch to dark mode
  - media: "(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
    scheme: slate
    primary: teal
    accent: light green
    toggle:
      icon: material/brightness-4
      name: Switch to light mode

仅深色主题。 只保留一条，并去掉 media 键：

YAML
palette:
  - scheme: slate
    primary: cyan
    accent: cyan

仅浅色主题。 同理使用 scheme: default。没有第二套 palette 时，页头的明暗切换按钮会消失。

docs.title: Logo 与图标
docs.text:
两者都在 theme 下配置，文件位于 docs/assets/：

YAML
theme:
  favicon: assets/favicon.svg
  logo: assets/logo.svg

用 workshop 自己的品牌文件替换这两个 SVG；保持文件名不变则无需改动配置。Logo 显示在页头，favicon 显示在浏览器标签页。

docs.title: Palette 之外
docs.text: primary/accent 覆盖不到的颜色（如背景色、组件边框）需要自定义 CSS，通过 extra_css 与 docs/overrides/ 实现；见自定义。

docs.title: 部署到 GitHub Pages
docs.text: 本页说明从空仓库到站点上线（https://<you>.github.io/<your-repo>/）的完整流程。模板承担了主要工作：GitHub Actions 工作流用 MkDocs 构建站点并发布到 gh-pages 分支。

docs.title: 第 1 步——从模板创建仓库
docs.text:
1. 打开 github.com/CedricHaskell/WorkshopTemplate。
  2. 点击 Use this template → Create a new repository。
  3. 填写仓库名。仓库名决定站点 URL：git-workshop 对应 https://<you>.github.io/git-workshop/。
  4. 可见性选择 Public。免费账号的 GitHub Pages 与 giscus 讨论区都要求仓库公开。
  5. 点击 Create repository。

为什么用 "Use this template" 而不是 "Fork"？

Fork 会保留与原仓库的关联，且需要手动启用 Actions 才会运行工作流。模板副本是一个独立的仓库，更适合需要大量定制的站点。

docs.title: 第 2 步——授予工作流部署权限
docs.text:
发布工作流使用内置的 GITHUB_TOKEN 把构建产物推送到 gh-pages 分支。新仓库默认只读权限，需要手动放开：

  1. 打开 Settings → Actions → General。
  2. 在 Workflow permissions 下选择 Read and write permissions。
  3. 点击 Save。

docs.title: 第 3 步——触发第一次构建
docs.text:
从模板创建仓库不属于 push 事件，因此工作流尚未运行。任意一次提交都会触发它：

  1. 打开 mkdocs.yml，点击铅笔图标进入编辑。
  2. 把 site_name: "Workshop Template" 改为 workshop 的名称。
  3. 同时更新 site_url 与 repo_url，见第 5 步。
  4. 提交修改（右上角按钮，例如 chore: rename site）。

随后 Actions 标签页会显示 publish site 工作流。如果页面提示工作流被禁用，点击页面上的按钮启用即可。

docs.title: 第 4 步——让 GitHub Pages 指向 gh-pages 分支
docs.text:
工作流把站点构建到 gh-pages 分支，还需要让 GitHub Pages 托管它：

  1. 打开 Settings → Pages。
  2. 在 Build and deployment → Source 中选择 Deploy from a branch。
  3. Branch 设为 gh-pages，目录设为 / (root)，点击 Save。

站点随后可在 https://<you>.github.io/<your-repo>/ 访问。

docs.title: 第 5 步——配置站点信息
docs.text:
至少更新 mkdocs.yml 中的以下字段：

YAML
site_name: "My Workshop"                    # 页头与浏览器标签页显示的名称
site_description: "A workshop about ..."    # 用于搜索引擎
site_author: "Your Name"
site_url: "https://<you>.github.io/<your-repo>/"   # 规范 URL 与语言切换器依赖此值
repo_url: "https://github.com/<you>/<your-repo>"
repo_name: "<your-repo>"

Logo文件默认是SSTIA图标。如果你需要用自己的图标，需要同时替换 docs/assets/ 中的：

  • logo.svg —— 页头 Logo，位于站点名称左侧
  • favicon.svg —— 浏览器标签页图标

最后，讨论区必须指向新仓库。模板默认配置的是原仓库，因此评论在副本上不会加载，直到配置被更新。具体步骤见讨论区。

docs.title: 本地预览（可选）
docs.text:
如需本地编辑与实时刷新：

Bash
git clone https://github.com/<you>/<your-repo>.git
cd <your-repo>
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate        # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
mkdocs serve

预览地址为 http://localhost:8000，保存即自动刷新页面。中文版位于 http://localhost:8000/zh/。

  • mkdocs serve —— 实时预览服务器（即上面的命令）
  • mkdocs build —— 把静态站点构建到 site/ 目录供检查
  • mkdocs build --strict —— 构建并在链接失效时报错；CI 对 pull request 执行的正是这一命令

docs.title: 自动化机制
docs.text:
模板在 .github/workflows/ 中附带两个工作流：

工作流 触发时机 作用 publish_site.yaml 每次推送到 main 安装依赖 → mkdocs build → 把 site/ 推送到 gh-pages 分支 health_check.yaml 每个 pull request 运行 mkdocs build --strict；存在失效链接的 PR 无法通过 CI

docs.title: 常见问题
docs.text: 现象 原因与处理 站点返回 404 Pages 尚未指向 gh-pages ——执行第 4 步 工作流从不运行 创建仓库后没有提交，或 Actions 被禁用 ——见第 3 步 工作流在部署步骤失败 工作流权限为只读 ——见第 2 步 站点上线但链接失效或指向错误域名 mkdocs.yml 中的 site_url 仍指向原模板 ——更新它（第 5 步） 每个页面评论区都报错 giscus 仍配置为模板仓库 ——见讨论区

docs.title: 适用人群
docs.text:
本模板面向 workshop 主讲人——设计并主持动手实践课程（hackathon、教程、培训）的讲师。它解决以下常见需求：

  • 以版本可控、便于分享的形式维护讲义；
  • 向参与者分发更新后的材料，而无需反复发送文件；
  • 为练习提供配套的讨论空间；
  • 同时维护同一份材料的英文与中文版本。

模板把讲义转换为静态网站，做法与 MIT's Missing Semester 一致：一个可搜索的站点容纳全部材料。

docs.title: 包含的功能
docs.text: 功能 说明 双语（EN / 中文） 每个页面都有两个完整版本，可从页头切换。中文站点位于 /zh/ 下 一键部署 推送到 main 即触发 GitHub Actions，自动构建并发布到 GitHub Pages 丰富的 Markdown 表格、代码块、提示框、任务列表、内容标签页、emoji、LaTeX 公式、Mermaid 图表 Material 主题 成熟的 Material for MkDocs 主题，支持明暗模式、标签页与搜索 图片与视频 模板自带的示例文件（image_demo.png、video_demo.mp4）演示媒体嵌入方法 讨论区 每页一条评论线程，由 giscus 与 GitHub Discussions 提供支持 交互式组件 md_in_html 扩展允许嵌入任意 HTML/CSS/JS——见小游戏 Demo CI 健康检查 每个 pull request 运行 mkdocs build --strict，链接失效即构建失败

docs.title: 前置条件
docs.text:
要求很低：

  • 一个 GitHub 账号（免费）；
  • 基础的 Markdown——会写 # 标题 和 **加粗** 即可完成大部分工作，其余见 Markdown 基础。

Python 并非必需：所有编辑都可以在 GitHub 网页编辑器中完成，由 Actions 负责构建。只有在需要本地预览时才要安装 Python 环境。

docs.title: 文档结构
docs.text:
文档按顺序组织，但每页都自成一体：

  1. 快速上手——部署与仓库结构（即本节）
  2. 内容编写——撰写页面：Markdown、配色、媒体、双语内容
  3. 讨论区——为参与者配置评论
  4. 高级功能——自定义：主题覆盖、钩子、插件、内嵌组件

承载本文档的网站就是由模板构建的。阅读时可以对照仓库：文中描述的每个特性都对应 docs/ 与 mkdocs.yml 中的真实文件。

docs.title: 下一步
docs.text: 部署自己的副本 →

docs.title: 结构总览
docs.text:
完整的仓库布局：

Text Only
.
├── .github/workflows/
│   ├── publish_site.yaml      # 推送到 main → 构建站点 → 部署到 gh-pages 分支
│   └── health_check.yaml      # PR 时 → mkdocs build --strict（链接失效即失败）
│
├── docs/                      # ← 所有内容都在这里
│   ├── en/                    # 英文源（默认语言 → 站点根目录）
│   │   ├── index.md           #   首页
│   │   ├── about.md
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── zh/                    # 中文源（→ 站点的 /zh/）
│   │   ├── index.md           #   与 docs/en/ 逐页对应
│   │   └── ...
│   ├── assets/                # 共享静态文件（两种语言共用）
│   │   ├── images/image_demo.png    # 媒体教程的示例图片
│   │   ├── videos/video_demo.mp4    # 媒体教程的示例视频
│   │   ├── favicon.svg              # 浏览器标签页图标
│   │   └── logo.svg                 # 页头 Logo
│   ├── javascripts/
│   │   └── mathjax.js         # MathJax 配置（每个页面都会加载）
│   ├── overrides/
│   │   └── comments.html      # giscus 讨论区模板（见讨论区一节）
│   └── scripts/
│       └── hooks.py           # 构建钩子，例如把 sitemap.xml 复制进 /zh/
│
├── mkdocs.yml                 # ← 核心配置：导航、主题、插件、i18n
├── requirements.txt           # 固定的 Python 依赖（CI 与本地开发共用）
├── CONTRIBUTING.md
├── LICENSE
└── README.md

docs.title: 两个部分：docs/ 与 mkdocs.yml
docs.text:
• docs/ 存放内容——Markdown 文件与素材。
  • mkdocs.yml 存放其余一切——站点名称、主题、配色、插件与导航。GitHub Action 运行 mkdocs build 时读取该文件，把 docs/ 转换成 site/ 里的静态站点。

docs.title: mkdocs.yml 内部
docs.text: 配置段 作用 site_name / site_url / repo_url 站点标识、规范 URL、仓库链接 theme Material 主题配置：明暗 palette、导航 features（标签页、返回顶部、搜索）、Logo/图标，以及指向 docs/overrides 的 custom_dir markdown_extensions Markdown 方言：表格、公式、emoji、Mermaid 代码块、提示框——即 Markdown 基础 页演示的全部内容 extra alternate——语言切换器条目（English → .，简体中文 → zh/）；以及全局 JavaScript（MathJax、Mermaid） plugins search（全文搜索）、mkdocs-video（视频嵌入）、i18n（双语构建）、minify（压缩 HTML） nav 导航即站点结构。只有列在此处的页面才会被构建。

docs.title: 双语构建的原理
docs.text:
i18n 插件（mkdocs-static-i18n）配置为 docs_structure: folder：

Text Only
docs/en/**  --（默认语言）-->  site/**      （英文站点）
docs/zh/**  ---------------->  site/zh/**   （中文站点）

由此产生两个结论：

  1. nav 中的路径是相对语言目录的。 条目 Home: index.md 在英文构建中解析为 docs/en/index.md，在中文构建中解析为 docs/zh/index.md。导航中从不出现语言前缀。
  2. docs/assets/ 是共享的。 两种语言的构建都会引用它；MkDocs 会自动重写相对路径，因此中文页面引用的图片能正确指向共享的 assets/ 目录。只需写 ../assets/images/…，在两种语言下都有效。

中文的导航标题来自插件配置中的 nav_translations；语言切换器来自 extra.alternate。详见双语支持。

docs.title: 补充说明
docs.text:
• 未列入 nav 的页面不会被构建。 MkDocs 只渲染导航可达的文件，因此新页面必须在 mkdocs.yml 中注册后才会出现；见新建页面。
  • docs/ 中的一切都会复制进站点。 因此 docs/scripts/hooks.py 与 docs/overrides/ 也会出现在发布的 site/ 目录中。这无害，但放在 docs/ 下的私有脚本将会公开。
